query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small boron micro-alloying addition (≈1.5 atomic % B) to the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy MM′X alloy, followed by rapid solidification and consolidation, will generate a thin, amorphous Mn–B–Si–Ge grain-boundary film that arrests transformation-induced cracking and raises the room-temperature compressive strength by ≥200 % (to ≥450 MPa) while retaining ≥90 % of the parent alloy’s magneto/barocaloric entropy change (ΔS and ΔT_ad within –10 % of baseline) under equivalent magnetic-field (≤2 T) or hydrostatic-pressure (≤1 GPa) operation.
generation.material_initial_state: Cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy MM′X alloy exhibiting large field- and pressure-driven first-order magnetostructural transition, ΔS ≈ –25 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 1 T but prone to spontaneous and cyclic-fatigue cracking; bulk ingot porosity <2 %; grain size 10–50 µm; negligible boron content.
generation.intervention: Vacuum induction melting with 1.5 at % elemental B addition, followed by melt-spinning (wheel speed ≈30 m s⁻¹) to refine grains and promote B segregation, and spark-plasma-sintering (SPS, 50 MPa, 900 °C, 5 min) to consolidate fully dense bulk.
generation.conditions: Caloric testing at 250–350 K across the first-order transition; magnetic fields up to 2 T; hydrostatic pressures up to 1 GPa; compressive loading at 10⁻³ s⁻¹ strain rate at 300 K.
generation.structural_mediator: Nanometre-thin amorphous (Mn,Fe)(B,Si,Ge) intergranular films decorating refined (~0.5–2 µm) grains.
generation.mechanism: 1) Boron segregates to grain boundaries during rapid solidification, forming ductile amorphous intergranular films that blunt and deflect cracks arising from the 3–4 % volume change of the magnetostructural transition. 2) Fine grains reduce stress concentrations and distribute transformation strains more uniformly. 3) The low concentration of B leaves the valence-electron count and lattice parameters almost unchanged, preserving the first-order transition and its associated large entropy/adiabatic-temperature changes.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the unmodified alloy, the B-modified material will show: • Quasi-static compressive strength ≥450 MPa (≥200 % increase) before fracture. • Fracture strain doubled (≥1.0 %). • Magnetic and barocaloric entropy change (ΔS) and adiabatic ΔT within –10 % of baseline values; transition temperature shift ≤5 K. • Cyclic pressure-cycling life (>10³ cycles to 0.5 GPa) at least fivefold longer.
generation.baseline: As-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy: compressive strength ≈150 MPa, fracture strain ≈0.4 %, ΔS ≈ –25 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 1 T, ΔT_ad ≈ 3.5 K, transition ~295 K, failure within <200 pressure cycles at 0.5 GPa.
generation.boundary: Effect expected for B additions between 0.5–3 at % and grain sizes ≤5 µm produced by rapid solidification + SPS; larger B contents or coarser grains may depress ΔS significantly (>15 %) or embrittle via boride precipitation; pressures >1 GPa or very high cycling rates (>1 Hz) may negate the benefit.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of strength gain and exact tolerance of ΔS to boron content depend on segregation efficiency; thermal conductivity change is not predicted due to insufficient prior data; possible formation of brittle MB compounds at B >3 at % could offset benefits.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two 20 g alloy batches: (a) baseline composition, (b) baseline +1.5 at % B. Process both identically via melt-spinning (30 m s⁻¹) and SPS consolidation (50 MPa, 900 °C, 5 min). Machine cylindrical specimens (Ø3 mm×6 mm) and caloric coupons (3×3×6 mm).
measurements: Room-temperature quasistatic compression curves to failure
X-ray diffraction and TEM for grain size and amorphous-film detection
Magnetization vs temperature (5–305 K, 1 T) for ΔS via Maxwell relation
Adiabatic temperature change ΔT_ad under 2 T and 1 GPa
Pressure-cycling life tests (0–0.5 GPa, 0.1 Hz) until 10 % drop in ΔS
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if: (1) Compressive strength increase <100 % over baseline OR fracture strain increases <25 %; OR (2) |ΔS_B – ΔS_baseline| >10 % at identical field/pressure; OR (3) Transition temperature shift >5 K; OR (4) Pressure-cycling life improvement <2×.
